title: Microsoft Purview Audit: what the unified audit log records, how long it keeps it and what it costs
summary: The Dataverse inspection control overstates its role requirement: Microsoft says anyone can view the configuration, while System Administrator or System Customizer is required to change it. The documented paths, commands, retention limits and explicitly reported documentation disagreements are otherwise supported.

claims.claim: In the Microsoft Purview portal, select Audit > Start recording user and admin activity to enable auditing.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true enables auditing in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Use PowerShell to turn on auditing ... Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell. ... Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal audit search path is Audit > Search.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog in Exchange Online PowerShell supports -StartDate, -EndDate, -UserIds, -Operations and -ResultSize for audit searches.
claims.quote:
Search-UnifiedAuditLog
    -EndDate <ExDateTime>
    -StartDate <ExDateTime> ... [-Operations <String[]>] ... [-ResultSize <Int32>] ... [-UserIds <String[]>]

claims.claim: Audit > Search in the Microsoft Purview portal is the UI counterpart to programmatic audit search.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/security/auditLog/queries creates an audit search query through Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: Create a new auditLogQuery object. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/auditLog/queries

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal retention policy creation path is Audit > Create audit retention policy.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... Select Create audit retention policy, and then complete the following fields on the flyout page:

claims.claim: New-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy supports -Name, -RecordTypes, -RetentionDuration and -Priority in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: New-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy -Name "Microsoft Teams Audit Policy" -Description "One year retention policy for all Microsoft Teams activities" -RecordTypes MicrosoftTeams -RetentionDuration TenYears -Priority 100

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center path is Security > Compliance > Auditing > environment > Set up auditing > Turn on auditing.
claims.quote: select Security > Compliance. ... Select the Auditing tile. ... Select the environment ... Select Set up auditing. In the Auditing pane, select Turn on auditing.

claims.claim: The documented v9.2 organizations GET query reads the five listed environment audit settings without changing them.
claims.quote:
GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations?$select=
auditsettings,
isauditenabled,
auditretentionperiodv2,
isuseraccessauditenabled,
useraccessauditinginterval HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: The unified audit log records user and admin operations across Microsoft services.
claims.quote: Your organization's unified audit log captures, records, and retains thousands of user and admin operations performed in dozens of Microsoft services and solutions.

claims.claim: An audited user or admin activity generates an audit record.
claims.quote: When a user or admin performs an audited activity, the system generates an audit record and stores it in the audit log for your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Audit has Standard and Premium tiers.
claims.quote: The following table compares the key capabilities available in Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium). Audit (Premium) includes all Audit (Standard) functionality.

claims.claim: Audit Standard is enabled by default for organizations with the appropriate subscription, subject to the SMB and trial exceptions stated later.
claims.quote: Audit (Standard) is enabled by default for all organizations with the appropriate subscription.

claims.claim: Audit Standard retains current audit records for 180 days.
claims.quote: In Audit (Standard), the system retains records for 180 days, which means you can search for activities that occurred within the past six months.

claims.claim: Audit Premium adds audit log retention policies.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) builds on the capabilities of Audit (Standard) by providing audit log retention policies

claims.claim: Audit Premium supports retention up to one year.
claims.quote: Create customized audit log retention policies to retain audit records for longer periods, up to one year

claims.claim: Audit Premium retention can extend to 10 years with the required add-on license.
claims.quote: up to 10 years for users with the required add-on license

claims.claim: Audit Premium adds intelligent insights.
claims.quote: high-value intelligent insights

claims.claim: Audit Premium provides higher Office 365 Management Activity API bandwidth.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) includes higher bandwidth access to the Office 365 Management Activity API, which provides faster access to audit data.

claims.claim: Dataverse auditing is configured at environment, table and column levels, with table and column auditing set separately.
claims.quote: You can configure auditing at three levels: environment, table, and column. First, turn on auditing at the environment level. To log data changes in a table, turn on auditing for the table and for the column.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Retention follows the user's licence
claims.claim: Audit retention and searchability depend on the license assigned to the user who performed the activity.
claims.quote: The length of time that an audit record is retained (and searchable in the audit log) depends on your Office 365 or Microsoft 365 Enterprise subscription, and specifically the type of the license that is assigned to specific users.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Logging can be off
claims.claim: Auditing is not enabled by default for Business Basic, Business Standard and Business Premium SMB licenses and must be enabled manually.
claims.quote: Auditing isn't enabled by default for Small and Medium Business (SMB) licenses, including Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Business Standard, and Business Premium.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Logging can be off
claims.claim: Auditing is not enabled by default for unmanaged tenants using enterprise license free trials and must be enabled manually.
claims.quote: unmanaged tenants that use free trials of enterprise licenses don't have auditing enabled by default. In both these cases, you must manually enable auditing for your organization.

claims.claim: Purview audit searches return no results when auditing is turned off.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog returns no results when auditing is turned off.
claims.quote: Running the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.claim: The Office 365 Management Activity API cannot access the organization's audit data when auditing is turned off.
claims.quote: If you turn off auditing in Microsoft 365, you can't use the Office 365 Management Activity API or Microsoft Sentinel to access auditing data or logs for your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft Sentinel cannot access the organization's audit data when auditing is turned off.
claims.quote: If you turn off auditing in Microsoft 365, you can't use the Office 365 Management Activity API or Microsoft Sentinel to access auditing data or logs for your organization.

claims.claim: Audit requires an appropriate organization subscription providing access to audit search.
claims.quote: Licensing for Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium) requires the appropriate organization subscription that provides access to the audit log search tool

claims.claim: Audit also requires the per-user licensing needed to log and retain audit records.
claims.quote: and per-user licensing that's required to log and retain audit records.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: One year retention
claims.claim: One-year retention requires Office 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Purview Suite or an E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on for the user generating the audit record.
claims.quote: the user who generates the audit log ... must have an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license or a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.claim: Ten-year retention needs an additional per-user 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on on top of Premium licensing.
claims.quote: In addition to the required licensing for Audit (Premium) ... a user must be assigned a 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on license to retain their audit records for 10 years.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: How they interact
claims.claim: Purview pay-as-you-go requires linking the Microsoft 365 tenant to an active Azure subscription for billing.
claims.quote: The billing mechanisms are Azure based, so you must associate your Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.

claims.claim: The Copilot audit page says Microsoft applications including Security Copilot, Copilot in Fabric and Copilot Studio custom applications are included in Audit Standard.
claims.quote: All Microsoft applications, including Microsoft Copilots like Microsoft Security Copilot, Copilot in Microsoft Fabric, and custom applications built using Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry are included in Audit Standard.

claims.claim: Get started lists Fabric, Security Copilot and Copilot Studio among non-Microsoft 365 AI data requiring pay-as-you-go, conflicting with the Copilot audit page.
claims.quote: you must enable pay-as-you-go billing for your organization. This data type includes Copilot in Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Security Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and any connected or cloud AI application.

claims.claim: The Copilot audit page names the billing unit but gives no per-record rate.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-copilot "rate" "billing"; opened audit-copilot and searched its full fetched text for rate, price, $, cost and billing. It describes records ingested but states no monetary rate.

claims.quote: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled ... A value of True for the UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled property indicates that auditing is turned on.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Logging can be off
claims.claim: The same property's value is always False when Get-AdminAuditLogConfig is run in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Although the Get-AdminAuditLogConfig cmdlet is also available in Security & Compliance PowerShell, the UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled property is always False, even when auditing is turned on.

claims.claim: Each Dataverse audit record is stamped with the active retention period when written.
claims.quote: Each audit log is stamped with the currently active retention period.

claims.claim: The admin guide says changing the retention period does not change existing records, while the page also reports its conflicting Security-page guidance.
claims.quote: Changing the retention period here doesn't change the retention period for already existing records.

claims.claim: The admin guide also says the Security page auditing option can apply retention to existing logs.
claims.quote: Use the Security page auditing option to set the retention policy. This option provides the flexibility to apply the retention policy to existing logs.

claims.claim: The developer configuration reference says ApplyRetentionToExistingLogs is ignored.
claims.quote: ApplyRetentionToExistingLogs | Apply new retention policy to existing audit records. | No, is ignored.

claims.claim: Portal audit search requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.claim: Audit cmdlet access requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs in the Exchange admin center.
claims.quote: To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: The Audit Reader and Audit Manager role groups provide audit-search roles by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Microsoft Purview portal Role groups page assigns these roles to the Audit Reader and Audit Manager role groups.

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Creating audit retention policies requires Organization Configuration.
claims.quote: You need the Organization Configuration role in the Microsoft Purview portal to create or modify an audit retention policy.

claims.claim: Changing Dataverse auditing requires System Administrator, System Customizer or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: You must have a system administrator or system customizer role or equivalent permissions to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Inspecting Dataverse environment audit settings and retention needs System Administrator or System Customizer.
claims.quote: Anyone can view the configuration, but you must have the System Administrator or System Customizer role to change the settings.
claims.fix: In controls[4].note and the rendered Dataverse row, replace 'Needs System Administrator or System Customizer.' with 'Changing these settings needs System Administrator or System Customizer; anyone can view the configuration.' Keep the existing read-only REST qualification.

claims.claim: An organization can have up to 50 audit log retention policies.
claims.quote: Your organization can have up to 50 audit log retention policies.

claims.claim: The default audit retention policy cannot be modified.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) in Microsoft Purview provides a default audit log retention policy for all organizations. You can't modify this policy.

claims.claim: A custom audit retention policy overrides the default policy.
claims.quote: All custom audit log retention policies (created by your organization) take priority over the default retention policy.

claims.claim: Lower audit retention policy priority numbers take precedence.
claims.quote: A lower value indicates a higher priority.

claims.claim: Audit controls record and expose activities rather than restricting the underlying activities.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard) enables you to log and search for audited activities to support your forensic, IT, compliance, and legal investigations.

claims.claim: Data policies, rather than auditing, govern how Copilot Studio agents connect to data and services.
claims.quote: Data policies let you govern how agents connect and interact with data and services, both within and outside your organization.

claims.claim: The documented new-customer Purview pay-as-you-go enablement flow is marked preview.
claims.quote: In this procedure, you enable the Microsoft Purview pay-as-you-go features by associating your Microsoft 365 tenant with an Azure subscription for billing purposes. ... This featue is in preview.

claims.claim: Get-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy lists audit retention policies for reviewing their priorities.
claims.quote: Use the Get-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell to view audit log retention policies.
